why: The workflows that must have RUN on the head commit of every open pull request.
This list exists because a pull request can show a screen full of green checks
while the workflow that actually runs the gates never started. Measured on
2026-09-07: pull request #105 reported 19 checks, all green but the one
expected red, and the CI workflow - gates, meter, workflow-hardening - had not
run at all, because ci.yml is filtered to `branches: [main, stable]` and the
pull request was opened on a stacked branch. Three of the twenty-four open
pull requests were in that state; the gate as it stood caught one, the only
The requirement deliberately does NOT depend on the pull request's base. A
list derived from each workflow's own `branches:` filter would reproduce the
defect's own logic and conclude that a pull request missing CI was never
supposed to have it. What gates a change is a property of the repository,
Both directions are checked. Every name below must exist as the `name:` of a
workflow file, or the sweep stops at COULD NOT MEASURE rather than accusing
every pull request of missing a workflow that was merely renamed. And every
workflow file triggered by `pull_request` must appear in one of the two lists,
so a new gating workflow cannot be added and quietly go unrequired.

required.why: the gates, the battery suite, the meter and the workflow hardening scan. If this did not run, nothing about the change was measured.
G7 protected paths, the declared-issue extraction and the shard verdict. It is the only workflow with no base filter, which is why its presence alone proves nothing about CI.

not_required_note: A `pull_request`-triggered workflow belongs here when its absence is not a

touch. Each entry needs a `why`, for the same reason an accepted coverage gap
